verdict.reason: M188 is functionally credible and realizes the exact K7 group bound, but its standalone frontend is 3.898062% larger than M184 while retaining only 99.911221% of K8 schedule throughput. It is therefore a necessary K7 selector proof point, not a winning frontend. M189 is justified only to determine whether the seven-lane arithmetic saving exceeds the selector and compactor cost.

m189_decision_rule.screen_basis: standalone M184 plus M185 versus standalone M188 plus prospective M189, same 3.0 ns exclusions
m189_decision_rule.warning: This is a standalone-sum screen only. A final decision requires a flattened composed issue island because synthesis can share or duplicate logic across the boundary.

P0: Do not promote M188 alone as the selected frontend: it loses 3.837262% schedule-throughput/area to M184 K8 at the same 3.0 ns logic-only screen.
M189 must include the actual eight-bank-to-seven-lane compactor and seven-lane signed accumulator, not a prepacked seven-lane input that hides routing cost.

Build a flattened M188 plus M189 issue island and compare it with a matched flattened K8 issue island. Require one accepted group per cycle and total K7 area below the throughput-adjusted K8 threshold before admitting a hardware-density win.
P1: Replay the frozen M187 payloads through the composed RTL or an exact transaction bridge; current M188 VCS proves policy and protocol but not all 120 payloads in RTL.
Report selector/compactor timing separately. M188 adds 12 mapped logic levels over M184 and has only 0.0002 ns ideal-clock setup slack at 3.0 ns.

Carry forward M186's reset/stale-response P0 into the composed response protocol by adding response identity/epoch or a flush-ack quarantine; M188 itself has no response port and cannot close that issue.
P2: After a winning flat screen, run Formality and PT/SAIF/PTPX with the same exact netlist identity. Do not infer energy from 12.5% nominal lane width.
Keep 1.807375x explicitly labeled as a conditional frontend schedule-throughput/logic-area ratio versus M180 K4, never as FC2, FFN, network, physical, or system speedup.
